Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Misra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Applicant-Complainant has approached this Court through this application under Section 482 Code
of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the impugned orders dated 24.11.2023 and 12.7.2023 passed
by Additional Sessions Judge/ Fast Track Court No.1, Etawah in Sessions Trial No. 214 of 2019,
titled State Vs. Ujjwal Porwal and others, arising out of Case Crime No. 420 of 2019, under Sections
366, 452, 376 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District Etawah.

entities.text: State Vs. Ujjwal Porwal and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant has argued that after commencement of trial, prosecution is in process of examining its witnesses and the defence/ accused is relying upon certain photographs to confront the witnesses, but as the negatives of the photographs have not been produced on record of the trial court, therefore, the said photographs cannot be used.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that in this regard, an application was moved by the applicant for restraining the accused from cross-examining the prosecution witness with the said material, but the trial court has wrongly dismissed the said application on the ground that the issues raised by the prosecution/ informant Rajeev Kumar Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151482435/
1 shall be decided at the final stage.

entities.text: Rajeev Kumar Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant further submits that Section 231 Cr.P.C. provides for evidence by prosecution and at that stage, the defence evidence cannot be accepted, therefore, the impugned orders warrant interference by this Court.
During the course of hearing, it is not disputed by learned counsel that photographs relied upon by the accused are not part of the final report.
However, according to learned counsel, the accused had also relied upon the said material while seeking bail.

After hearing the learned counsel for applicant and considering his submissions, this Court does not find any merit in this application as the prosecution cannot seek restraint against the defence to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses as in terms of Section 146 Indian Evidence Act, 1872, any question can be put to the prosecution witnesses in cross-examination to test the veracity of his or her deposition.

At the stage of cross-examination of prosecution witnesses, the accused also discloses the defence and if, certain photographs are being relied upon by the defence counsel, he cannot be restrained to confront the prosecution witnesses with the said material, as it would violate his right to fair trial.

A perusal of the impugned order would reveal that material now sought to be prohibited for usage against the P.W.-4, is the same, which has already been utilized against the other prosecution witnesses.

Further, it is also noticed by the trial court in the impugned order dated 24.11.2023 that previously, a similar application moved on behalf of the prosecution seeking restraint of use of an affidavit of the victim was also dismissed.

Concededly, it is not a case where the material relied upon by the defence is irrelevant to the case set up by the prosecution, therefore, this Court has no hesitation in holding that the impugned orders passed by the trial court are based upon correct appreciation of the material on record.
The impugned orders do not warrant any interference by this Court.
The application fails and is hereby, dismissed.

Order Date :- 14.3.2024 P.S.Parihar  Rajeev Kumar Mishra vs State Of U.P. And Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151482435/
